resources.content:
# TestNG - Part 3

<Section>

## Concepts

<IndexList>
    <IndexItem href="testing-the-home-page">Testing the Home Page</IndexItem>
    <IndexItem href="comprehensive-web-page-testing">Comprehensive Web Page Testing</IndexItem>
    <IndexItem href="testng-test-suites">TestNG Test Suites</IndexItem>
    <IndexItem href="running-testng-xml">Running TestNG.xml</IndexItem>
</IndexList>

</Section>

<Section>

## Introduction

In the previous unit, we learned about more advanced features of TestNG, including how to write a login failure case, how to add priority to our test cases, how to use the `@BeforeMethod` and `@AfterMethod` annotations, and how to provide data to test methods using `@DataProvider`. 

In this unit, we will dive deeper and explore topics such as parallel testing, XML suite files, TestNG XML files, the hierarchy of TestNG annotations. 

<MultiLineNote>

Click [here](https://new-assets.ccbp.in/frontend/content/qa-testing/NxtTrendzTestNGAutomation1.zip) to download the initial code for this project.

Make sure to update the PATH\_TO_CHROMEDRIVER variable in the **LoginPageTest** class with the correct path to the location of the ChromeDriver executable on your local machine


</MultiLineNote>

</Section>



<Section>
## Testing the Home Page
The first step in testing the home page is to ensure that we can successfully log in. The initial code provided sets up the WebDriver and navigates to the login page. It then logs in with valid credentials and navigates to the home page. From there, we can start testing the home page elements.

Advancement of the initial code will involve adding tests for the "Shop Now" button and the Heading Element on the home page. We will use the `@Test` annotation to define these tests and the Assert class to validate the functionality and appearance of these elements.

After successful login, the next important part of a web application to test is the home page. The home page is where users interact with the application the most. Therefore, it's crucial to ensure that all elements on the home page are functioning as expected.

Here is how we can advance our initial code to test the home page:

```java
@Test(priority = 2)
    public void loginWithInvalidCredentials() {

        WebElement usernameEl = driver.findElement(By.id("username"));
        usernameEl.sendKeys("rahul");

        WebElement passwordEl = driver.findElement(By.id("password"));
        passwordEl.sendKeys("rahul@2022");

        WebElement loginButtonEl = driver.findElement(By.className("login-button"));
        loginButtonEl.submit();

   }

```

In the above code, we first log in using valid credentials. After successful login, we wait for a specific element on the home page to be visible. This element should be unique to the home page. Once the element is visible, we assert that the home page is loaded.
</Section>

<Section>

## Comprehensive Web Page Testing
When we test large applications, it's a best practice to organize tests for different parts into separate files. This not only makes your tests more manageable but also keeps them neat and easy to handle. In the context of our NxtTrendz application, the first step to reach the homepage involves a successful login. Therefore, we need to create a test case to ensure the login process works correctly.

Advancement of the initial code will involve creating a new test class for the home page tests. This class will include methods for each test case, and we will use the `@BeforeMethod` and `@AfterMethod` annotations to set up and tear down the WebDriver for each test.

Comprehensive web page testing involves testing all the elements of a web page. This includes links, forms, images, text, etc. It's important to ensure that all these elements are working as expected to provide a smooth user experience.

Here is how we can advance our initial code to perform comprehensive web page testing:

```java
import org.testng.annotations.AfterMethod;

public class HomePageTest {
  @Test
  public void clickOnShopNowButton() {...}
  @Test
  public void checkHeadingElement() {...}
  @AfterMethod
  public void tearDown() {
    driver.close();
  }
}
```

In the above code, we first log in using valid credentials. After successful login, we test the links and images on the web page. We check if each link is working and if each image is loaded. We can add similar code to test other elements of the web page.

</Section>

<Section>
## TestNG Test Suites

A Test Suite is a collection of test cases that are intended to test a specific behavior of the software/application. TestNG Test Suites are a powerful feature that allows us to execute multiple test cases together efficiently. To execute TestNG Test Suites, we need to create a TestNG XML file to handle multiple test classes.

Advancement of the initial code will involve creating a testng.xml file that includes both the login page tests and the home page tests. We will use the , , and  elements to define the test suite.

TestNG allows us to create test suites, which are collections of test cases that are intended to be executed together. Test suites are defined in a XML file. This allows us to easily manage and run multiple test cases.

Here is how we can advance our initial code to create a TestNG test suite:

```xml
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "http://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd" >
<suite name="My Test Suite">
    <test name="Login Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.mycompany.myproject.LoginPageTest" />
        </classes>
    </test>
    <test name="Home Page Test">
        <classes>
            <class name="com.mycompany.myproject.HomePageTest" />
        </classes>
    </test>
</suite>


```
In the above XML, we define a test suite named "My Test Suite". This suite contains two tests: "Login Test" and "Home Page Test". Each test contains a class that contains the test methods.
</Section>

<Section>

## Running TestNG.xml

There are multiple ways to run a testng.xml file. Here are three common methods: Using testng.xml file, Maven, Command line. Right-click on the testng.xml file in the Project explorer panel and click on Run 'testng.xml'.

Advancement of the initial code will involve running the test suite using the testng.xml file. We will use the TestNG plugin in our IDE to do this.

After defining our test suite in a XML file, we can run it using TestNG. This allows us to easily execute multiple test cases with a single command.

Here is how we can advance our initial code to run a TestNG.xml:


```java
<!DOCTYPE suite SYSTEM "https://testng.org/testng-1.0.dtd" >
<suite name="Sample Test Suite">
   <test name="Sample Test" >
     <classes>
        <class name="SampleTest1" />
        <class name="SampleTest2" />
     </classes>
   </test>
</suite>


```


</Section>

<Section>

### Summary

In this unit, we learned how to test other parts of a web application, such as the home page, and how to conduct comprehensive web page testing. We also learned about TestNG test suites and how to run them using TestNG.xml. These skills are crucial in ensuring that our web application is functioning as expected and providing a smooth user experience.

# TestNG - Part 4
## Concepts Limitations of Sequential Execution Introduction to Parallel Testing Parallel Testing in the NxtTrendz Application Comparison: With and Without Parallel Testing Introduction to TestNG Reports Generating and Displaying index.html & emailable-report.html Reports How to customize TestNG Report Advantages of Reports in TestNG
## Introduction In the previous unit, we learned about testing Home page functionalities by writing required test cases for the home page, we took two test cases and ran our tests on them. Then we learned how we can run multiple tests simultaneously using a file called as `TestNG.xml`. We also learnt about the `TestNG.xml` file is a configuration file used in the TestNG testing framework. It allows testers to define the test execution behavior, specify the test classes or methods to be included or excluded, set test dependencies, and configure various other testing parameters. In this unit, we will explore more advanced features of TestNG. We will learn about Parallel Testing, Limitations of step-by-step validation of our test cases in sequential execution, how to get TestNG Reports, types of TestNG Reports and Examination of index.html and emailable-report.html Click [here](https://new-assets.ccbp.in/frontend/content/qa-testing/NxtTrendzTestNGAutomation2.zip) to download the initial code for this project.
## 1. Limitations of Sequential Execution While sequential execution allows for step-by-step validation of our test cases, there is a significant limitation: `the time taken for testing`. Each test case runs one after the other, adding up the individual times for all test cases. For instance, executing hundreds of test cases for features like login, product listing, and shopping cart in our application can take a significant amount of time.
## 2. Introduction to Parallel Testing Parallel testing is a process where multiple tests are executed simultaneously in different thread processes. TestNG provides built-in support for parallel testing, which can be configured using the `TestNG XML` file. `TestNG XML` is the test suite configuration file in TestNG, it helps us organize our tests by defining test suites, grouping test cases in TestNG, and running them under one XML file. Before exploring parallel test execution in TestNG, let's identify the areas within the code that can be parallelized. Parallel testing triggers with the help of the keyword `"parallel"` and accepts the following `keywords (values)` in TestNG: - **Methods:** This will run parallel tests on all @Test methods in TestNG. - **Tests:** All test cases inside the tag will run with this value. - **Classes:** All test cases inside the XML classes will run in parallel. - **Instances:** This value will run all the test cases in parallel inside the same instance. We can also set the number of threads we wish to allocate during execution using the thread-count attribute. TestNG has a default thread value of **5**, but we can adjust this number based on our needs and system capabilities.
## 3. Parallel Testing in the NxtTrendz Application To add parallel execution at the class level, we add `parallel = "classes"` to the `` tag in the TestNG XML configuration file. `parallel` attribute ensures TestNG runs all test methods in the same `` tag in a single thread, while different `` tags can run in separate threads. The number of threads you choose for parallel testing depends largely on your system's capabilities and your specific testing requirements If you have four test classes and you want them all to run in parallel, you would ideally set the thread count to 4. However, keep in mind that you should consider the capabilities of your system. If your machine doesn't have enough resources (like CPU and memory) to handle four threads running concurrently, you might experience slowdowns, errors, or unpredictable behavior #### Adding Parallel Attribute: To add parallel execution at the class level, we add `parallel = "classes"` to the tag. #### Syntax ```xml ``` #### Code ```xml ``` In the above given example code the thread count is 2, allowing two threads for execution. These threads run 2 test methods in parallel.
## 4. Comparison: With and Without Parallel Testing ### Without Parallel Testing: #### output: If we see the `Without parallel testing` example above, tests are run one after the other `(HomePageTest is executed after the LoginAndHomePageTest)`. Think of it like reading a book from start to finish, page by page. You can't start reading the next page until you've finished the current one. This can be time-consuming, especially if there are many tests to run. ### With Parallel Testing: #### output: If we see the `With parallel testing` example above, Parallel testing is like having multiple people read different parts of the same book at the same time. One person might start at the beginning, another person might start in the middle, and a third person might start at the end `(HomePageTest and LoginPageTest executing parallely)`. They each read a section of the book, and together, they finish reading the entire book much faster than one person could alone. In the context of testing, this means multiple tests are run at the same time, each one on a separate thread, making the entire process quicker and more efficient. ### Advantages of parallel testing: - *Efficiency:* Parallel testing allows multiple tests to be run simultaneously, which can significantly reduce the total time required for testing. - *Faster Feedback:* With parallel testing, feedback is quicker because tests are being executed simultaneously. This allows any issues to be identified and resolved more quickly. ### Disadvantages of parallel testing: - *Increased Complexity:* Coordinating and managing parallel tests can be more complex than sequential testing, especially when dealing with dependencies between tests. - *Requires Careful Planning:* Test cases need to be carefully designed to be independent of each other when run in parallel. If test cases are interdependent, running them in parallel can lead to unexpected results or failures.
## 5. Introduction to TestNG Reports Every time we run tests, a report is generated. This report indicates which tests passed and which didn't, helping us see what's working and what needs to be fixed. TestNG provides built-in reporting features, and without any extra configuration, it will generate default reports after test execution. The TestNG will generate the default report. When we execute `testng.xml` file, we will get **test-output** folder in that folder for reporting in TestNG. If we don't get the default reports, we need to configure them by following the below instructions in settings. - Click on `Edit Configurations` in `Run` tab. - Click `Listeners`. - Click `Use Default Reporters`. - First click on `Apply` and then click `OK`. - Execute `testng.xml` file. - In the `test-output` folder, we can find the `index.html` and `emailable-report.html` reports, they provide a comprehensive summary of the test execution and are useful for understanding the results without having to create custom reports.
## 6. Generating and Displaying index.html & emailable-report.html Reports ### index.html: - For executing `index.html` right click on the `index.html` and click on `Open in Browser` then select `Chrome` - A new window is opened in the Browser with the `index.html` Report like below, then click on the `passed methods(show)` - Now a detailed Report of testcases run on our project will be opened like below. The `index.html` file provides a detailed overview of the test execution, and it includes the following information: 1. **Suite Name**: Name of the test suite that was executed. 2. **Test Name**: Name of the individual tests within the suite. 3. **Class Name**: Name of the classes that contain the test methods. 4. **Method Name**: Name of the individual test methods. 5. **Status**: Outcome of each test method, such as passed, failed, or skipped. 6. **Start Time and End Time**: Execution start and end time for the test methods. 7. **Duration**: Total time taken to execute each test method. 8. **Exception Information**: Details about any exceptions or errors that occurred during the test execution, including stack traces. 9. **Links to Detailed Reports**: The index page typically has links to more detailed reports, such as the `groups.html`, which provides information about the groups of tests. ### emailable-report.html: As the name suggests, this is a more concise HTML report designed to be suitable for email distribution. It contains essential information about the test execution in a compact format, making it easier to share with stakeholders who may want a quick overview without all the details. You can find this report in the `test-output` directory as well. - For executing `emailable-report.html` right click on the `emailable-report.html` and click on `Open in Browser` then select `Chrome`. - A new window is opened in the Browser with the `emailable-report.html` Report like below. The `emailable-report.html` file is designed to provide a concise summary of the test execution, suitable for sharing via email. It includes: 1. **Suite Name**: Name of the test suite. 2. **Test Name**: Name of the individual tests within the suite. 3. **Total Methods**: The total number of test methods executed. 4. **Passed Methods**: The number of test methods that passed. 5. **Failed Methods**: The number of test methods that failed. 6. **Skipped Methods**: The number of test methods that were skipped. 7. **Duration**: Total time taken for the test execution. 8. **Start Time and End Time**: Overall start and end time for the test suite.
## 7. How to customize TestNG Report TestNG's reporting feature is valuable, but it may not always fit our needs. Sometimes, we might want to simplify the reports, change their appearance, or even convert them into different formats like PDF or Excel We have the ability to generate reports by utilizing the ITestListener Interface. ITestListener Interface is used when we want to create a real-time report while running a set of test cases in a TestNG suite. If we want a report on each individual test case, we implement the ITestListener interface. It allows us to know the status of each test case by overriding methods like onTestFailure, onTestStart, and onTestSkipped. In simple terms, it helps us keep track of what's happening with our tests as they run The `ITestListener` interface in TestNG provides several methods that allow you to track the status and behavior of your tests. Here's a breakdown of the methods and what each one does: 1. **`onTestStart(ITestResult result)`**: This method is called when a test method starts executing. You can use it to perform any setup or logging that needs to happen right when a test begins. 2. **`onTestSuccess(ITestResult result)`**: This method is called when a test method completes successfully. It's a place where you might log success messages or handle anything that should happen specifically when a test passes. 3. **`onTestFailure(ITestResult result)`**: This method is called when a test method fails. You can use this to log the failure or handle other actions that should occur when a test does not pass. 4. **`onTestSkipped(ITestResult result)`**: If a test method is skipped, this method will be called. This can be used to log the skipping or handle other specific logic related to skipped tests. 5. **`onTestFailedButWithinSuccessPercentage(ITestResult result)`**: This method is called when a test method fails but is within the success percentage set for the tests. It's a specialized method that can be used to handle these partial success scenarios. 6. **`onStart(ITestContext context)`**: Called before a `` tag is run in the XML file. Useful for setting up things that need to be in place for the entire test run within that `` tag. 7. **`onFinish(ITestContext context)`**: This method is called after all the tests inside a `` tag have run. It can be used for teardown or final reporting related to the entire set of tests within that `` tag. By implementing these methods in a class that implements the `ITestListener` interface, you can have very fine-grained control over what happens during the entire lifecycle of your test execution. **ITestContext** is an interface in TestNG that provides various details about the execution of a set of tests. It's like a bundle that contains information and functionality around the tests being run. Here's a simple explanation for it: Imagine you're conducting a series of science experiments, and you have a logbook where you write down things like the name of the experiment, the time you started, any special equipment you're using, and notes on what happens during the experiment. In TestNG, `ITestContext` is like that logbook for your tests. When your tests are running, `ITestContext` keeps track of information like: - **Name of the Test**: What this particular set of tests is called. - **Start Time**: When the tests began running. - **End Time**: When the tests finished running. - **Failed Tests**: Information about any tests that didn't pass. - **Passed Tests**: Information about the tests that did pass. - **Skipped Tests**: Information about any tests that were skipped and didn't run at all. - **Attributes**: A place where you can store and retrieve custom information that you want to keep track of during your tests. In the methods `onStart(ITestContext context)` and `onFinish(ITestContext context)`, you get access to this "logbook," and you can read from it or write to it depending on what you need to do. - **`onStart(ITestContext context)`**: This method is like opening the logbook when you're about to start the experiments. You can set up things here that you'll need for all the experiments. - **`onFinish(ITestContext context)`**: This is like closing the logbook when you're done with all the experiments. You can look back at your notes and see what happened, or clean up anything that needs to be put away. So, `ITestContext` is a handy tool that helps you keep track of what's going on when you're running a bunch of tests, just like a logbook helps you keep track of what's happening when you're conducting a series of experiments. Certainly! Here's how you can modify those steps for your specific `NxtTrendzApplications`: 1. **Create a Class Named NxtTrendzReport**: Start by defining a new class called `NxtTrendzReport` in your project. This class will be responsible for handling the customized reporting for your `NxtTrendzApplications`. 2. **Implement the iTestListener Interface**: In the `NxtTrendzReport` class, implement the `iTestListener` interface. By doing this, you're telling the class to use a set of methods that help in customizing the test reporting. 3. **Implement the Methods of iTestListener**: Within the `NxtTrendzReport` class, you'll need to provide the specific functionality for the various methods in `iTestListener`. These methods help you to capture events like when a test starts, fails, or finishes, so you can tailor the reports to your needs. By following these steps, you'll have a custom reporting system in place for your `NxtTrendzApplications`, allowing you to generate reports that meet your specific requirements. Certainly! Here's an example of how you might set up a custom reporting class for your NxtTrendz Applications using the `iTestListener interface`. First, let's define the `NxtTrendzReport` class that implements the `ITestListener` interface. #### NxtTrendzReport.java ```java import org.testng.ITestContext; import org.testng.ITestListener; import org.testng.ITestResult; public class NxtTrendzReport implements ITestListener { @Override public void onTestStart(ITestResult result) { System.out.println("Test Started: " + result.getName()); } @Override public void onTestSuccess(ITestResult result) { System.out.println("Test Success: " + result.getName()); } @Override public void onTestFailure(ITestResult result) { System.out.println("Test Failed: " + result.getName()); } @Override public void onTestSkipped(ITestResult result) { System.out.println("Test Skipped: " + result.getName()); } @Override public void onStart(ITestContext context) { System.out.println("Starting Test Suite"); } @Override public void onFinish(ITestContext context) { System.out.println("Finishing Test Suite"); } } ``` The `getName()` method in the provided code is a method of the `ITestResult interface` in TestNG. It's used to get the name of the test method that's currently being executed. 4. **Add NxtTrendzReport as a Listener in Test Method Class**: In the class where your test methods for `NxtTrendzApplications` are defined, add the `NxtTrendzReport` class as a listener. This step connects your custom reporting class to the tests, so the reporting methods are called at the right times during test execution. #### HomePageTest.java ```java import org.openqa.selenium.WebDriver; import org.openqa.selenium.chrome.ChromeDriver; import org.openqa.selenium.WebElement; import org.openqa.selenium.By; import org.openqa.selenium.support.ui.ExpectedConditions; import org.openqa.selenium.support.ui.WebDriverWait; import java.time.Duration; import org.testng.annotations.Test; import org.testng.annotations.BeforeMethod; import org.testng.annotations.AfterMethod; import org.testng.Assert; import org.testng.annotations.Listeners; @Listeners(NxtTrendzReport.class) public class HomePageTest { public WebDriver driver; @BeforeMethod public void setup() { System.setProperty("webdriver.chrome.driver", "/home/nxtwavetechhari/Downloads/chromedriver_linux64/chromedriver"); driver = new ChromeDriver(); driver.get("https://rahulnxttrendz.ccbp.tech/login"); WebElement usernameEl = driver.findElement(By.id("username")); usernameEl.sendKeys("rahul"); WebElement passwordEl = driver.findElement(By.id("password")); passwordEl.sendKeys("rahul@2021"); WebElement loginButtonEl = driver.findElement(By.className("login-button")); loginButtonEl.submit(); } @Test public void clickOnShopNowButton() { WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, Duration.ofSeconds(10)); WebElement shopNowEl = wait.until(ExpectedConditions.visibilityOfElementLocated(By.className("shop-now-button"))); shopNowEl.click(); String expectedUrl = "https://rahulnxttrendz.ccbp.tech/products"; String currentUrl = driver.getCurrentUrl(); Assert.assertEquals(expectedUrl, currentUrl, "URLs do not match"); } @Test public void checkHeadingElement() { WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, Duration.ofSeconds(10)); WebElement element = wait.until(ExpectedConditions.visibilityOfElementLocated(By.className("home-heading"))); Assert.assertTrue(element.isDisplayed(), "Element is not visible"); } @AfterMethod public void tearDown() { driver.quit(); } } ``` #### LoginPageTest.java ```java import org.openqa.selenium.WebDriver; import org.openqa.selenium.chrome.ChromeDriver; import org.openqa.selenium.WebElement; import org.openqa.selenium.By; import org.openqa.selenium.support.ui.ExpectedConditions; import org.openqa.selenium.support.ui.WebDriverWait; import java.time.Duration; import org.testng.annotations.Test; import org.testng.annotations.BeforeMethod; import org.testng.annotations.AfterMethod; import org.testng.annotations.DataProvider; import org.testng.Assert; import org.testng.annotations.Listeners; @Listeners(NxtTrendzReport.class) public class LoginPageTest { public WebDriver driver; @DataProvider public Object[][] loginData() { return new Object[][] { { "praneetha", "praneetha@2021" }, { "rahul", "rahul@2021" } }; } @BeforeMethod public void setup() { System.setProperty("webdriver.chrome.driver", "/home/nxtwavetechhari/Downloads/chromedriver_linux64/chromedriver"); driver = new ChromeDriver(); driver.get("https://rahulnxttrendz.ccbp.tech/login"); } @Test(priority = 1, dataProvider = "loginData") public void loginWithValidCredentials(String username, String password) { WebElement usernameEl = driver.findElement(By.id("username")); usernameEl.sendKeys(username); WebElement passwordEl = driver.findElement(By.id("password")); passwordEl.sendKeys(password); WebElement loginButtonEl = driver.findElement(By.className("login-button")); loginButtonEl.submit(); String expectedUrl = "https://rahulnxttrendz.ccbp.tech/"; WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, Duration.ofSeconds(10)); wait.until(ExpectedConditions.urlToBe(expectedUrl)); String currentUrl = driver.getCurrentUrl(); Assert.assertEquals(expectedUrl, currentUrl, "URLs do not match"); } @Test(priority = 2) public void loginWithInvalidCredentials() { WebElement usernameEl = driver.findElement(By.id("username")); usernameEl.sendKeys("rahul"); WebElement passwordEl = driver.findElement(By.id("password")); passwordEl.sendKeys("rahul@2022"); WebElement loginButtonEl = driver.findElement(By.className("login-button")); loginButtonEl.submit(); // Wait for the Error message to be loaded WebDriverWait wait = new WebDriverWait(driver, Duration.ofSeconds(10)); //Wait until elements are displayed wait.until(ExpectedConditions.visibilityOfElementLocated(By.className("error-message"))); WebElement errorMessageEl = driver.findElement(By.className("error-message")); String errorMessage = errorMessageEl.getText(); Assert.assertEquals(errorMessage, "*username and password didn't match"); } @AfterMethod public void tearDown() { driver.close(); } } ``` #### Run the testng.xml file ```xml ``` #### Output:
## 8. Advantages of Reports in TestNG **1.Understanding Results:** TestNG reports provide a clear and concise overview of the test execution. They show the number of tests passed, failed, and skipped, along with other details such as the time taken to run each test. This information can help testers and developers understand the results of the test execution, identify any problematic areas, and take necessary actions. **2.Tracking Progress:** Over time, as tests are repeatedly run, the reports can be used to track the progress of the testing process. You can see how many tests are passing now compared to previous runs, whether new issues are being introduced, or if existing issues have been resolved. This can provide valuable insight into the quality and stability of the software over time. **3.Sharing Information:** TestNG reports, particularly the emailable-report.html, are designed to be easily shared among team members and stakeholders. This allows everyone involved in the project to stay updated on the current status of the testing process. It's a great way to keep everyone on the same page, especially in distributed teams. **4.Finding Errors:** In case of test failures, the reports provide detailed information about the error or exception that caused the test to fail, including the stack trace. This information is invaluable for debugging and can help developers find and fix errors more efficiently. **5.Support for Different Formats:** TestNG supports different formats for reports, such as HTML and XML. The HTML reports are easy to read and understand, while the XML reports can be used for further processing, like converting to other formats, or feeding into continuous integration servers or other tools. **6.Customization:** TestNG allows customization of reports. If the default reports do not meet your needs, you can create a custom listener to generate reports in a format that is more suitable for your specific requirements. This might include adding additional information to the report, changing the layout, or even generating reports in completely different formats. This can make TestNG a very flexible tool for reporting on test execution.
### Summary - TestNG supports parallel test execution, which can significantly reduce the total test execution time. However, it requires careful consideration of thread safety and shared resources. - TestNG reporting mechanisms provide detailed and easily shareable reports, facilitating team collaboration, tracking progress, identifying errors, and customizing as per specific needs. - TestNG's default reports, `index.html` and `emailable-report.html`, are both rich in information and serve different purposes. They offer comprehensive insights into test execution, facilitating a better understanding of test results, which can be shared across the team or stakeholders. - TestNG's reporting feature is valuable, but it may not always fit our needs. Sometimes, we might want to simplify the reports, change their appearance, or even convert them into different formats like PDF or Excel

### Exercises IPL Dashboard App Test Fitness App Test Meetup App Test 2 Tech Talks App Test _Note: Set up the project and practice this exercise in your local IDE(IntelliJ)._
### IPL Dashboard App Test In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the IPL Dashboard App. ### Prerequisites - Install IntelliJ IDEA Community IDE Version 2018.3.6. - Install OpenJDK 11 and complete the configuration. - Install a Browser Driver(Chrome Driver). - Setup a Selenium project with the name `IplDashboardAppTest`. - Update the Build in `pom.xml`. Refer to previous exercises for reference. You can refer to this [Reading Material](https://learning.ccbp.in/qa-automation-testing/course?c_id=cf952b35-27ab-4b1e-a6de-44227f22806c&s_id=f5c19277-3889-4e63-b631-c06c088d612c&t_id=6a935df7-2c93-477c-b505-3ae0aabcf9a2#31-installing-ide) to complete the above prerequisites. ### Test Instructions - Create a `HomePageTest` class and write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the Heading of the Home Page - Navigate to the URL `https://qaipldashboard.ccbp.tech/` - Verify if the IPL logo is displayed - _use Assertions_, - If the IPL logo is not displayed, print "IPL logo is not displayed" - Verify the Heading text of the page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `IPL Dashboard` - If the Heading text does not match the expected text, print "Heading text does not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the list of Teams in the Home Page - Navigate to the URL `https://qaipldashboard.ccbp.tech/` - Verify the order and the list of Teams in the Home Page - _use Assertions_ - Order: _"Royal Challengers Bangalore", "Kolkata Knight Riders", "Kings XI Punjab", "Chennai Super Kings", "Rajasthan Royals", "Mumbai Indians", "Sunrisers Hyderabad", "Delhi Capitals"_ - if the order and the list of Teams do not match, print "Order and list of Teams do not match" - Close the browser window.
- Create a `TeamPageTest` class and write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the Team Page - Navigate to the URL `https://qaipldashboard.ccbp.tech/` - Wait and click the fourth team in the list. - Wait and verify the navigation to the registration page - _use Assertions_, - Expected URL: `https://qaipldashboard.ccbp.tech/team-matches/CSK` - If the current URL does not match the expected URL, print "URLs do not match" - Wait and verify if the CSK team image is displayed - _use Assertions_, - If the image is not displayed, print "Team image is not displayed" - Verify the latest match team - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `Royal Challengers Bangalore` - If the latest team does not match the expected text, print "Latest match team name does not match" - Verify the count of the recent matches - _use Assertions_ - Expected count: `13` - If the count does not match the expected count, print "Count does not match" - Close the browser window.
### Running Tests - Use Parallel testing with _parallel_ attribute values as **classes** and _thread-count_ required for the tests to run parallel.
### Fitness App Test In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the Fitness App. ### Prerequisites - Install IntelliJ IDEA Community IDE Version 2018.3.6. - Install OpenJDK 11 and complete the configuration. - Install a Browser Driver(Chrome Driver). - Setup a Selenium project with the name `FitnessAppTest`. - Update the Build in `pom.xml`. Refer to previous exercises for reference. You can refer to this [Reading Material](https://learning.ccbp.in/qa-automation-testing/course?c_id=cf952b35-27ab-4b1e-a6de-44227f22806c&s_id=f5c19277-3889-4e63-b631-c06c088d612c&t_id=6a935df7-2c93-477c-b505-3ae0aabcf9a2#31-installing-ide) to complete the above prerequisites. ### Test Instructions - Create a `LoginPageTest` class and write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the submission with empty input fields - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Click the "Login" button. - Wait and verify the error message - _use Assertions_, - Expected text: `Invalid user ID` - If the error message does not match the expected text, print "Error text with empty input fields does not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the submission with empty User ID field - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Enter the text `231225` in the "PIN" field. - Click the "Login" button. - Wait and verify the error message - _use Assertions_, - Expected text: `Invalid user ID` - If the error message does not match the expected text, print "Error text with empty input field do not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the submission with empty PIN field - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Enter the text `142420` in the "User ID" field. - Click the "Login" button. - Wait and verify the error message - _use Assertions_, - Expected text: `Invalid PIN` - If the error message does not match the expected text, print "Error text with empty input field do not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the submission with invalid PIN - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Enter the text `142420` in the "User ID" field. - Enter the text `123456` in the "PIN" field. - Click the "Login" button. - Wait and verify the error message - _use Assertions_, - Expected text: `User ID and PIN didn't match` - If the error message does not match the expected text, print "Error text with invalid PIN do not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the successful login - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Enter the text `142420` in the "User ID" field. - Enter the text `231225` in the "PIN" field. - Click the "Login" button. - Wait and verify the navigation to the home page - _use Assertions_, - Expected URL: `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/` - If the current URL does not match the expected URL, print "URLs do not match" - Close the browser window.
- Create a `HomePageTest` class and write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the Homepage Heading - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Enter the text `142420` in the "User ID" field. - Enter the text `231225` in the "PIN" field. - Click the "Login" button. - Wait until the web driver navigates to the home page, - Home Page URL: `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/` - Verify the Description text of the home page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `"The only bad workout is the one that didn't happen."` - If the Description text does not match the expected text, print "Description text does not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the Logout functionality - Navigate to the URL `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login` - Enter the text `142420` in the "User ID" field. - Enter the text `231225` in the "PIN" field. - Click the "Login" button. - Wait until the web driver navigates to the home page, - Home Page URL: `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/` - Click the "Logout" button. - Verify the navigation to the login page - _use Assertions_, - Expected URL: `https://qafitnessapp.ccbp.tech/gym/login/` - If the current URL does not match the expected URL, print "URLs do not match" - Close the browser window.
- Create a `FitnessAppReport` class that implements the `ITestListener` and add it as a listener to the our Test classes (`LoginPageTest` and `HomePageTest`). - In the `FitnessAppReport` class, override the below methods | Method | Action | | :------------ | :---------------------------------------- | | onTestStart | Prints "Test Started: \" | | onTestSuccess | Prints "Test Success: \" | | onTestFailure | Prints "Test Failed: \" | | onTestSkipped | Prints "Test Skipped: \" | | onStart | Prints "Starting Test Suite" | | onFinish | Prints "Finished Test Suite" | ### Running Tests - In the `testng.xml` keep the `LoginPageTest` and `HomePageTest` classes in separate `` XML elements. - Use Parallel testing with _parallel_ attribute values as **tests** and _thread-count_ required for the tests to run parallel.
### Meetup App Test 2 In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the Meetup App. ### Prerequisites - Install IntelliJ IDEA Community IDE Version 2018.3.6. - Install OpenJDK 11 and complete the configuration. - Install a Browser Driver(Chrome Driver). - Setup a Selenium project with the name `MeetupAppTest2`. - Update the Build in `pom.xml`. Refer to previous exercises for reference. You can refer to this [Reading Material](https://learning.ccbp.in/qa-automation-testing/course?c_id=cf952b35-27ab-4b1e-a6de-44227f22806c&s_id=f5c19277-3889-4e63-b631-c06c088d612c&t_id=6a935df7-2c93-477c-b505-3ae0aabcf9a2#31-installing-ide) to complete the above prerequisites. ### Test Instructions - Create a `WelcomePageTest` class and write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the UI of the Welcome Page - Navigate to the URL `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` - Verify if the App logo is displayed - _use Assertions_, - If the App logo is not displayed, print "App logo is not displayed" - Verify the Heading text of the page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `Welcome to Meetup` - If the Heading text does not match the expected text, print "Heading text does not match" - Verify the Description text of the page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `Please register for the topic` - If the Description text does not match the expected text, print "Description text does not match" - Verify if the Meetup image is displayed - _use Assertions_, - If the Meetup image is not displayed, print "Meetup image is not displayed" - Close the browser window.
Test the Functionality of the Welcome Page - Navigate to the URL `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` - Click the "Register" button. - Verify the navigation to the registration page - _use Assertions_, - Expected URL: `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/register` - If the current URL does not match the expected URL, print "URLs do not match" - Close the browser window.
- Create a `RegistrationPageTest` class and write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the UI of the Registration Page - Navigate to the URL `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` - Click the "Register" button to navigate to the registration page. - Verify if the App logo is displayed - _use Assertions_, - If the App logo is not displayed, print "App logo is not displayed" - Verify if the Register image is displayed - _use Assertions_, - If the Register image is not displayed, print "Register image is not displayed" - Verify the Heading text of the page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `Let us join` - If the Heading text does not match the expected text, print "Heading text does not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the Functionality of the Registration Page with empty name field - Navigate to the URL `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` - Click the "Register" button to navigate to the registration page. - Click the "Register Now" button. - Verify the error message - _use Assertions_, - Expected text: `Please enter your name` - If the error message does not match the expected text, print "Error text with empty input field does not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the Functionality of the Registration Page with valid inputs - Navigate to the URL `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` - Click the "Register" button to navigate to the registration page. - Test the functionality of the Registration Page using various inputs from the given dataset. **Dataset** | Name | Option Value | Option Text | | :---: | :----------------------: | :--------------------: | | Jack | ARTS\_AND\_CULTURE | Arts and Culture | | Jerry | CAREER\_AND\_BUSINESS | Career and Business | | John | EDUCATION\_AND\_LEARNING | Education and Learning | | Jim | FASHION\_AND\_BEAUTY | Fashion and Learning | | Jane | GAMES | Games | - Enter the name in the "NAME" field - Select the corresponding option from the "TOPICS" dropdown. - Click the "Register Now" button. - Verify the navigation to the registration page - _use Assertions_, - Expected URL: `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` - If the current URL does not match the expected URL, print "URLs do not match" - Verify the Heading text of the page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `Hello ` - If the Heading text does not match the expected text, print "Heading text does not match" - Verify the Description text of the page - _use Assertions_ - Expected text: `Welcome to ` - If the Description text does not match the expected text, print "Description text does not match" - Close the browser window.
### Running Tests - In the `testng.xml` keep the `RegistrationPageTest` and `WelcomePageTest` classes in separate `` XML elements. - Use Parallel testing with _parallel_ attribute values as **tests** and _thread-count_ required for the tests to run parallel.
### Tech Talks App Test In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the TechTalk App. ### Prerequisites - Install IntelliJ IDEA Community IDE Version 2018.3.6. - Install OpenJDK 11 and complete the configuration. - Install a Browser Driver(Chrome Driver). - Setup a Selenium project with the name `TechTalksAppTest`. - Update the Build in `pom.xml`. Refer to previous exercises for reference. You can refer to this [Reading Material](https://learning.ccbp.in/qa-automation-testing/course?c_id=cf952b35-27ab-4b1e-a6de-44227f22806c&s_id=f5c19277-3889-4e63-b631-c06c088d612c&t_id=6a935df7-2c93-477c-b505-3ae0aabcf9a2#31-installing-ide) to complete the above prerequisites. ### Dataset | Name | Talk | | :----: | :-------------------------------------------------: | | Ronny | Blockchain: Secure, Decentralized Data Exchange. | | Albert | Cloud Computing: Flexible, Scalable Infrastructure. | | Antony | AI: Intelligent Systems Transforming Industries. | | Henry | IoT: Connecting Devices, Enhancing Efficiency. | | Helen | AR/VR: Immersive Digital Experiences. | ### Test Instructions - Write the test cases for the below test scenarios, _Note: The test cases should be executed in the same order as given below_
Test the talks counter - Navigate to the URL `https://qatechtalksapp.ccbp.tech/` - Add the talks from the dataset table. - For each talk added, verify whether the talk count is updated respectively. - If the count does not match the expected count, print "Talks count do not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the talk initials - Navigate to the URL `https://qatechtalksapp.ccbp.tech/` - Add the talks from the dataset table individually - _use DataProvider_. - Verify whether the username initials are displayed properly. - If the initial does not match the expected initial, print "Initial do not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the talks order - Navigate to the URL `https://qatechtalksapp.ccbp.tech/` - Add the talks from the dataset table. - Verify whether the username and the talks are displayed in the order they are added. - If the order does not match the expected order, print "Order does not match" - If the talk does not correspond to the username, print "Talk does not correspond to the username" - Close the browser window.
Test the like buttons - Navigate to the URL `https://qatechtalksapp.ccbp.tech/` - Add the talks from the dataset table. - For each like button clicked, verify whether the total talks liked are as expected - If the liked count does not match the expected count, print "Likes count do not match" - Close the browser window.
Test the delete buttons - Navigate to the URL `https://qatechtalksapp.ccbp.tech/` - Add the talks from the dataset table. - For each talks deleted, verify whether the total talks count is as expected - If the talk count does not match the expected count, print "Talks count do not match" - Close the browser window.
- Create a `TechTalksAppReport` class that implements the `ITestListener` and add it as a listener to the our Test class. - In the `TechTalksAppReport` class, override the below methods | Method | Action | | :------------ | :---------------------------------------- | | onTestStart | Prints "Test Started: \" | | onTestSuccess | Prints "Test Success: \" | | onTestFailure | Prints "Test Failed: \" | | onTestSkipped | Prints "Test Skipped: \" | | onStart | Prints "Starting Test Suite" | | onFinish | Prints "Finished Test Suite" | ### Running Tests - Use Parallel testing with _parallel_ attribute values as **classes** and _thread-count_ required for the tests to run parallel.
Once you have completed all the exercises, click on the "Mark as Completed" button.

Define the locators for the Home page > - App image > - App heading > - App description > - Name input field > - Comment input field > - "Add Comment" button > - Comment counter text > - Comment counter element() > - Initial text > - Comment username text > - Comment text > - List of like buttons > - List of liked comments > - List of delete buttons
Define the methods for performing actions on the elements > - Find the app image > - Get the text content of the app heading > - Get the text content of the app description > - Enter a text in the name input field > - Enter a text in the comment input field > - Click the "Add Comment" button > - Add a comment with a specified name and comment > - Get the text content of the comment counter text > - Get the comment count > - Get the text content of the initial text > - Get the username text at a specified index > - Get the comment text at a specified index > - Click the like button at a specified index > - Get the count of the liked comments > - Click the first delete button

Test the Comments App UI >- Navigate to the URL `https://qacommentsapp.ccbp.tech/` >- Verify if the App image is displayed - _use Assertions_, > - If the App image is not displayed, print "App image is not displayed" >- Verify the Heading text of the app - _use Assertions_ > - Expected text: `Comments` > - If the Heading text does not match the expected text, print "Heading text does not match" >- Verify the Description text of the app - _use Assertions_ > - Expected text: `Say something about 4.0 Technologies` > - If the Description text does not match the expected text, print "Description text does not match" >- Verify the Comments count text of the app - _use Assertions_ > - Expected text: `0Comments` > - If the Comments count text does not match the expected text, print "Comments count text does not match" >- Close the browser window.
Test the comment counter >- Navigate to the URL `https://qacommentsapp.ccbp.tech/` >- Add the comments from the dataset table. >- For each comment added, verify whether the comment count is updated respectively. > - If the count does not match the expected count, print "Comments count do not match" >- Close the browser window.
Test the comment initials >- Navigate to the URL `https://qacommentsapp.ccbp.tech/` >- Add the comments from the dataset table individually - _use DataProvider_. >- Verify whether the username initials are displayed properly. > - If the initial does not match the expected initial, print "Initial do not match" > - The initial is displayed in capitals irrespective of the case of the username >- Close the browser window.
Test the comment order >- Navigate to the URL `https://qacommentsapp.ccbp.tech/` >- Add the comments from the dataset table. >- Verify whether the username and the comment are displayed in the order they are added. > - If the order does not match the expected order, print "Order does not match" > - If the comment does not correspond to the username, print "Comment does not correspond to the username" >- Close the browser window.
Test the likes >- Navigate to the URL `https://qacommentsapp.ccbp.tech/` >- Add the comments from the dataset table. >- For each like button clicked, verify whether the total comments liked are as expected > - If the liked count does not match the expected count, print "Likes count do not match" >- Close the browser window.

Test the Functionality of the Registration Page with valid inputs >- Navigate to the URL `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` >- Click the "Register" button to navigate to the Registration page >- Test the functionality of the Registration Page using various inputs from the given dataset. > > **Dataset** > > | Name | Option Value | Option Text | > | :---: | :----------------------: | :--------------------: | > | Jack | ARTS\_AND\_CULTURE | Arts and Culture | > | Jerry | CAREER\_AND\_BUSINESS | Career and Business | > | John | EDUCATION\_AND\_LEARNING | Education and Learning | > | Jim | FASHION\_AND\_BEAUTY | Fashion and Learning | > | Jane | GAMES | Games | > > - Enter the name in the "NAME" field > - Select the corresponding option from the "TOPICS" dropdown. > - Click the "Register Now" button. > - Verify the navigation to the Welcome page - _use Assertions_, > - Expected URL: `https://qameetup.ccbp.tech/` > - If the current URL does not match the expected URL, print "URLs do not match" > - Verify the Heading text of the page - _use Assertions_ > - Expected text: `Hello ` > - If the Heading text does not match the expected text, print "Heading text does not match" > - Verify the Description text of the page - _use Assertions_ > - Expected text: `Welcome to ` > - If the Description text does not match the expected text, print "Description text does not match" >- Close the browser window.
### Running Tests - In the `testng.xml` keep the `RegistrationPageTest` and `WelcomePageTest` classes in separate `` XML elements. - Use Parallel testing with _parallel_ attribute values as **tests** and _thread-count_ required for the tests to run parallel.

Decrease the size of the Image.` > - If the expected text matches the actual text, print "Error text is as expected" > - Else, print "Error text is not as expected" > - Refresh the page. > - Click the "-" button twenty times, > - For every click, verify the width of the image, > - If the image width does not decrease by 5px, print "Sizing is not as expected". > - Click the "-" button. > - Verify the error text, > - Expected text: `Can't Visible. Increase the size of the Image.` > - If the expected text matches the actual text, print "Error text is as expected" > - Else, print "Error text is not as expected" > - If the image width changes as expected for both cases, print "Sizing is as expected".
Button Maker page > - Enter the text `blue` in the background color field. > - Enter the text `white` in the font color field. > - Enter the text `16px` in the font size field. > - Enter the text `bold` in the font weight field. > - Enter the text `15px` in the padding field. > - Enter the text `10px` in the border radius field. > - Verify if the enable checkbox, > - If the checkbox is not selected, print "Checkbox is not selected". > - Click the "Apply" button. > - Verify the following properties of the "Custom Button", > - Expected background color: `rgba(0, 0, 255, 1)` > - Expected font color: `rgba(255, 255, 255, 1)` > - Expected font size: `16px` > - Expected font weight: `700` > - Expected padding: `15px` > - Expected border radius: `10px` > - If all the expected properties matches the actual properties, print "Custom Button is displayed as expected" > - Else, print "Custom Button is not displayed as expected" > - Verify the "Custom Button" state, > - If the button is disabled, print "Error in Checkbox" > - Click the enable checkbox. > - Click the "Apply" button. > - Verify the "Custom Button" state, > - If the button is enabled, print "Error in Checkbox" > - If there is no error in the checkbox, print "Checkbox is working as expected".

# Introduction to BDD and Cucumber
## Concepts Behavior-Driven Development Cucumber Setting up Cucumber Project
## Introduction Till now we have created test cases, generated reports, created page objects etc. using Selenium with TestNG for testing our web application. While Selenium with TestNG and Java is a powerful combination for automation testing, it does present certain challenges: - Limited Collaboration - Technical Complexity **Limited Collaboration** In the software development process, there are various scenarios where non-technical stakeholders, such as business analysts, product owners, and even clients, might need to understand the tests. For example, - **Progress Tracking:** Reviewing tests to understand the progress of a particular feature or application - **Requirement Verification:** Business analysts and product owners review tests to ensure development aligns with system requirement **Technical Complexity** Writing tests using Java may require an understanding of complex programming concepts. This can be a barrier for those new to programming or non-technical stakeholders involved in the project. To overcome these challenges, there is an approach called Behavior-Driven Development. In this course we will learn what is Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) approach and how to implement using software tools like Cucumber. We will also learn how to use Cucumber with Selenium. Click [here](https://new-assets.ccbp.in/frontend/content/qa-testing/NxtTrendzTestsUsingCucumber.zip) to download the initial code for this project.
## 1. Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) is a software development approach that emphasizes collaboration between developers, testers, and business stakeholders. It focuses on defining the behavior of a software application in a way that is understandable by all stakeholders. In BDD, the tests are written in a language that is understandable to both technical and non-technical stakeholders: - Tests are written in plain descriptive English-type grammar - Tests are explained as a behavior of an application and are more user-focused **Advantages** - Test to Behavior: Shifting from thinking in "tests" to thinking in "behavior" - Collaboration Between Teams: Collaboration between Business stakeholders, Business Analysts, QA Team and developers There are different software tools that allow us to implement the BDD approach: - Cucumber - Specflow - Lettuce Let's understand what is Cucumber in detail. In this unit, we will be learning about how cucumber supports BDD.
## 2. Cucumber Cucumber is a tool that supports the BDD approach and acts as the bridge between the Software Engineer and non-tech stakeholders. Cucumber allows stakeholders to write and describe software behavior without needing to know the details of how that functionality is implemented. It uses a language called Gherkin for writing specifications/tests. ### 2.1. Gherkin Gherkin is a simple, natural language syntax used to describe the behavior of a software application in a way that is understandable by non-technical stakeholders. It is used in conjunction with Cucumber to define acceptance criteria and scenarios for a software feature. It uses a set of special keywords to define the application behaviour: - Feature: This represents a high-level business objective and provides context - Scenario: Defines a specific example or use case of the feature - Given: This sets up the context for the scenario. It's the starting point for the scenario - When: This defines the action that triggers the event - Then: This defines the expected outcome or result - And, But: These keywords are used to combine multiple given, when, or then steps Each feature in Gherkin corresponds to a real-world example of the behavior of the system. These features form the basis of our test cases. ### 2.2. Cucumber with Selenium Many organizations use Selenium for functional and regression testing. Selenium and Cucumber are a great combination when it comes to web application automation. Selenium provides the capability to interact with browsers, automating the execution of these behaviors across various browser combinations. Cucumber in Selenium is an open-source testing framework that supports Behavior Driven Development for testing the web applications. The Given-When-Then format of Gherkin can be mapped to Selenium commands, enhancing readability and maintainability.
## 3. Setting up Cucumber Project Let's learn step-by-step on how to set up Cucumber in IntelliJ IDEA. - Install Cucumber Plugin - Set up Cucumber with Selenium ### 3.1. Install Cucumber Plugin This usually involves downloading and installing the appropriate Cucumber libraries for our programming language For Java, this typically involves adding the Cucumber libraries to our project's build path - **Step 1**: Click on the `File` button on the top left corner of the IntelliJ IDE and select the settings option as shown in the below image. - **Step 2**: In the settings, select the `Plugins` option. Cick on the `Marketplace` tab and search as **Cucumber for Java** as shown in the below image. - **Step 3**: Click install as shown in the below image. - **Step 4**: Click restart as shown in the below image. ### 3.2. Set up Cucumber with Selenium This usually involves adding the necessary Selenium libraries to our project and setting up the necessary infrastructure (like the WebDriver) for running our tests The `pom.xml` is a configuration file used to add project dependencies. We can use MVN repository to get the dependencies for project. It is a centralized source of software artifacts, making it easier for developers to manage dependencies and build their projects. - **Step 1**: Search for [https://mvnrepository.com/](https://mvnrepository.com/) in the browser to open the MVN repository. - **Step 2**: In the search field, type **Cucumber-Java**. - **Step 3**: Now, click on the latest version `7.13.0`. - **Step 4**: Copy the Cucumber-Java dependency `7.13.0` ```text io.cucumber cucumber-java 7.13.0 ``` - **Step 5**: Paste the dependency in the `pom.xml` - **Step 6**: In the search field, type **Cucumber-TestNG**. - **Step 7**: Now, click on the latest version `7.13.0`. - **Step 8**: Copy the Cucumber-TestNG dependency `7.13.0` ```text io.cucumber cucumber-testng 7.13.0 ``` - **Step 9**: Paste the dependency in the `pom.xml` - **Step 10**: Now click on the reload button to get the dependencies downloaded. Now, we have Cucumber successfully installed in our project and ready to be used. In the next session, we will be writing our first project in Selenium using Cucumber.
### Summary - **Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)** is a software development approach that emphasizes collaboration between developers, testers, and business stakeholders. - **Cucumber** is a tool that supports the BDD approach and acts as the bridge between the Software Engineer and non-tech stakeholders. - **Gherkin** is a simple, natural language syntax used to describe the behavior of a software application in a way that is understandable by non-technical stakeholders. - Selenium and Cucumber are a great combination when it comes to web application automation.

### Nomadic Journeys Page Test

In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the scroll event.

### Prerequisites

- Install IntelliJ IDEA Community IDE  Version 2018.3.6.
- Install OpenJDK 11 and complete the configuration.
- Install a Browser Driver(Chrome Driver).
- Setup a Selenium project with the name `NomadicJourneysPageTest`.

You can refer to this [Reading Material](https://learning.ccbp.in/qa-automation-testing/course?c_id=cf952b35-27ab-4b1e-a6de-44227f22806c&s_id=f5c19277-3889-4e63-b631-c06c088d612c&t_id=6a935df7-2c93-477c-b505-3ae0aabcf9a2#31-installing-ide) to complete the above prerequisites.

### Steps to Automate

- Create a driver instance using WebDriver interface.
- Navigate to the URL `https://qanomadicjrny.ccbp.tech/`
- Scroll the page to the bottom.
- Wait until the `<h2>` element with text content `Marvel at the Wonders of Petra` is visible.
- Verify the count of the articles displayed.
    - If the count of the articles equals to 12, print `All 12 articles displayed`
    - Else, print `Few articles are missing...`
- Close the browser window.

</Section>

<Section>

### Projects Preview Page Test

In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the mouse hover event.

### Prerequisites

- Install IntelliJ IDEA Community IDE  Version 2018.3.6.
- Install OpenJDK 11 and complete the configuration.
- Install a Browser Driver(Chrome Driver).
- Setup a Selenium project with the name `ProjectsPreviewPageTest`.

You can refer to this [Reading Material](https://learning.ccbp.in/qa-automation-testing/course?c_id=cf952b35-27ab-4b1e-a6de-44227f22806c&s_id=f5c19277-3889-4e63-b631-c06c088d612c&t_id=6a935df7-2c93-477c-b505-3ae0aabcf9a2#31-installing-ide) to complete the above prerequisites.

### Steps to Automate

- Create a driver instance using WebDriver interface.
- Navigate to the URL `https://qapreviewpage.ccbp.tech/`
- Verify the initial background color of the "Fitness Library" card,
  - - Expected Background Color: `rgba(248, 250, 252, 1)`
    - If both expected and actual colors are the same, then print "Fitness Library Card Initial Background Color Verified"
    - Else, print "Fitness Library Card Initial Background Color Mismatched"
- Verify the initial background color of the "Country and Population" card,
  - - Expected Background Color: `rgba(248, 250, 252, 1)`
    - If both expected and actual colors are the same, then print "Country and Population Card Initial Background Color Verified"
    - Else, print "Country and Population Card Initial Background Color Mismatched"
- Perfom Hover action on "Fitness Library" card and verify its background color
    - Perform test that initial background color and the current background color are not the same.
    - If both expected and actual colors are not the same, then print "Fitness Library Card Background Color Verified on Hover"
    - Else, print "Fitness Library Card Background Color on Hover Mismatched"
- Perfom Hover action on "Country and Population" card and verify its background color
    - Perform test that initial background color and the current background color are not the same.
    - If both expected and actual colors are not the same, then print "Country and Population Card Background Color Verified on Hover"
    - Else, print "Country and Population Card Background Color on Hover Mismatched"
- Close the browser window.

</Section>

<Section>

### Book Manager Page Test

In this exercise, you will be automating the process of testing the drag and drop feature of the Book Manager Page.

- Capture a screenshot of the application and store it in the local directory

#Course-Exam: Automation Testing with Selenium
**Objective of the Course Exam:** The course exam aims to assess your understanding and knowledge of the course content and determine your performance in the respective course. It serves as a means to evaluate your readiness and proficiency in the subject matter.
**Eligibility Criteria:** To be eligible to attempt the course exam, each topic must be marked as complete. Double-check the course curriculum in your schedule to make sure each session and course item is marked as complete
**Grading:** Upon completion of each course, you will be assigned a course-wise exam, and your performance will be graded based on the following criteria: | Grade | Grade Point | Exam Score % |Exam Marks(60) | :---: | :-------: |:-------: |:-------: | | A | 10 | >80% | >=48 | | B | 8 | 60-80% | 36-47 | | C | 6 | 40-60% | 24-36 | | D | 4 | 20-40% | 12-24 | | E | 2 | <20% | <12 | For the Automation Testing with Selenium course exam ***achieve Grade A (min. 48/60 marks)***
**Cumulative Grade Calculation:** An overall cumulative grade will be assigned based on your performance across all courses within your chosen job track. The cumulative grade reflects your overall progress and success in the program.
Cumulative Grade = (Sum of all the course Grades present in the Job Track) / (Number of courses present in the job track)
**Course Exam Attempts:** You can attempt the course exam multiple times to improve your grade. Each attempt will allow you to demonstrate your understanding and enhance your performance. - It is crucial to maintain good grades throughout the program as it can increase the number of job opportunities available to you. - Recruiters will have access to your grades and performance during the program, and this information may be considered when evaluating candidates for job openings.
**IRC (Industry-Ready Certification) Eligibility Criteria:** To be eligible for the Industry-Ready Certification (IRC), you must fulfill the following criteria: - Achieve a ***cumulative grade of a minimum of 7.5/10*** - Complete all projects with given requirements and pass all plagiarism checks - Complete Project Verification & Viva - Please note that while your grades play a significant role in achieving IRC, they are not the sole determining factor. - Other factors, such as project performance, project verification, and viva, are also considered in evaluating your readiness for the industry.
**Refrain from Malpractice** Instances of **malpractice, cheating,** or **copying** during the course exams are taken seriously and may result in severe consequences, including but not limited to **disqualification from the exam, invalidation of exam results, invalidation of further Placement Support, or further disciplinary actions as per the program's policies**. - We urge you to **uphold the principles of honesty, integrity, and ethical conduct** throughout the exam. - Your individual efforts and genuine understanding of the course content are essential for your personal growth and success. - To ensure a fair and transparent examination environment, we expect all participants to adhere to the following guidelines: - Do not engage in any form of cheating, including but not limited to copying answers from others, using unauthorized materials, or seeking assistance from external sources during the exam. - Avoid communicating or exchanging information with other participants during the exam, whether in person or through online platforms. - Refrain from accessing unauthorized resources, websites, or applications that may provide an unfair advantage. - Use only the allowed resources, if any, as specified in the exam instructions. If specific materials or resources are permitted, ensure they are used within the defined boundaries.
**Aviod Technical issues** 1. Here is a document that will help you avoid technical issues when taking the course exam. 2. Attempting the Mock Practice Test to check your laptop/system supports the test environment.

Remember to prepare thoroughly for each course exam, review the course material, and seek clarification on any doubts before attempting the exam. All the Best!!
